problem_type: Multiple inline image results lost by URL-only response scanning
symptom: Compatible images responses containing b64_json could return only the first image through the known-shape fallback.
direct_cause: Generic result scanning recognized URLs but did not decode b64_json result fields.
class_root: The shared result-reading boundary did not normalize all supported inline media before ranking and collecting outputs.
internal_only_reason: Normalization reuses the existing b64_json contract and byte-sniffing helper; no new provider protocol is introduced.
invariants: Every result image is eligible for collection, not only array item zero
Input and reference branches remain excluded
Image payloads cannot satisfy video output contracts
Magic bytes determine the inline media type

door_reduction.why_not: Canvas execution, capability execution and polling remain separate callers of one shared reader; its definition and MIME conversion callers also remain necessary. Generated by door-map readTaskResponse and base64JsonToDataUrl.

generality_proof: All three production callers already use readTaskResponse. Normalizing inline candidates inside its scanner applies regardless of provider name, array length or sync versus query execution.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Normalize inline result candidates while retaining branch exclusions and media-kind filtering

recurrence.reason: Any compatible provider may return several inline images.

prevention.invariant: All valid result candidates enter the same selection boundary, while input branches stay excluded.
prevention.failure_mode: Invalid or wrong-kind bytes cannot become accepted generated assets; downstream byte certification remains required.
prevention.strategy: Decode b64_json candidates using the existing MIME helper before generic result ranking.

legacy_paths.rationale: Existing single-result extraction still serves other result shapes; its conversion helper is shared, not duplicated.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Internal response normalization; no dependency upgrade required.

migration: No persisted catalog or asset rewrite. Newly returned arrays use the corrected shared reader.
residual_risks: Real batch tests issue separate n=1 intents; n>1 array completeness is covered offline, not claimed as live upstream support.

verification.red: HEAD reader dynamically loaded from git show returned 1 of 2 base64 results; working reader returned 2. Mixed URL/base64 regression failed twice before normalization (with and without mapping).
verification.green: See scoped regression and real batch reports; no silent pixel transformation.
